source_text: Μὴ δή, ὦ ἀδελφοί, κακόν τι εἴπητε εἰς ἐκεῖνον τὸν ἐσταυρωμένον, μηδὲ χλευάσητε αὐτοῦ τοὺς μώλωπας, οἷς ἰαθῆναι πᾶσι δυνατόν, ὡς καὶ ἡμεῖς ἰάθημεν . Καλὸν γάρ, ἢν πεισθέντες τοῖς λόγοις περιτμηθῆτε τὴν σκληροκαρδίαν, ἥν οὐχὶ δι᾿ ὑμῶν ἐγγινομένην γνώμην ἔχετε, ἐπειδὴ εἰς σημεῖον ἦν δεδομένη, ἀλλ᾿ οὐκ εἰς δικαιοπραξίας ἔργον, ὡς οἱ λόγοι ἀναγκάζουσι. Συμφάμενοι οὖν μὴ λοιδορῆτε ἐπὶ τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ θεοῦ, μηδὲ Φαρισαίοις πειθόμενοι διδασκάλοις τὸν βασιλέα τοῦ Ἰσραὴλ ἐπισκώψητέ ποτε, ὁποῖα διδάσκουσιν οἱ ἀρχισυνάγωγοι ὑμῶν, μετὰ τὴν προσευχήν. Εἰ γὰρ ὁ ἁπτόμενος τῶν μὴ εὐαρέστων τῷ θεῷ ὡς ὁ ἁπτόμενος κόρης τοῦ θεοῦ , πολὺ μᾶλλον ὁ τοῦ ἠγαπημένου καθαπτόμενος . Ὅτι δὲ οὗτος αὐτός ἐστι, καὶ ἱκανῶς ἀποδέδεικται. Καὶ σιγώντων αὐτῶν εἶπον· Ἐγώ, ὦ φίλοι. καὶ τὰς γραφὰς λέγω νῦν ὡς ἐξηγήσαντο οἱ ἑβδομήκοντα· εἰπὼν γὰρ αὐτὰς πρότερον ὡς ὑμεῖς αὐτὰς ἔχετε, πεῖραν ὑμῶν ἐποιούμην πῶς διάκεισθε ἤδη τὴν γνώμην. Λέγων γὰρ τὴν γραφήν, ἣ λέγει· Οὐαὶ αὐτοῖς, ὅτι βεβούλευνται βουλὴν πονηρὰν καθ᾿ ἑαυτῶν εἰπόντες· ὡς ἐξηγήσαντο οἱ ἑβδομήκοντα ἐπήνεγκα· Ἄρωμεν τὸν δίκαιον, ὅτι δύσχρηστος ἡμῖν ἐστιν· ἐμοῦ ἐν ἀρχῇ τῆς ὁμιλίας καὶ εἰπόντος ὅπερ ὑμεῖς εἰρῆσθαι βούλεσθε, εἰπόντες· Δήσωμεν τὸν δίκαιον, ὅτι δύσχρηστος ἡμῖν ἐστιν . Ἄλλα δέ τινα ἐπράξατε, καὶ οὐ δοκεῖτέ μοι ἐνηκόως τῶν λόγων ἐπακηκοέναι. Ἀλλ᾿ ἐπεὶ καὶ νῦν ἤδη ἡ ἡμέρα πέρας ποιεῖσθαι μέλλει, πρὸς δυσμὰς γὰρ ἤδη ὁ ἥλιός ἐστι, καὶ ἔν τι προσθεὶς τοῖς εἰρημένοις παύσομαι· τοῦτο δ᾿ αὐτὸ καὶ ἐν τοῖς εἰρημένοις μοι ἐρρέθη, ἀλλὰ πάλιν αὐτὸ ἐπεξεργάσασθαι ἄν δίκαιον εἶναί μοι δοκεῖ.
pass_a_gloss: Do not, O brothers, speak anything bad against the one who was crucified, nor mock his bruises, by which it is possible for all to be healed, as we also have been healed. For it is good, if being persuaded by the words, you circumcise the hardness of heart, which you do not have because of your opinion, since it was given for a sign, but not for a work of righteousness, as the words compel. Therefore, having agreed, do not rail against the Son of God, nor, obeying the Pharisee teachers, ever despise the King of Israel, as your synagogue rulers teach after the prayer. For if the one touching the things not pleasing to God is like the one touching the daughter of God, much more the one touching the beloved. That this one is he, has been sufficiently demonstrated. And when they were silent, I said: I, O friends, now speak the scriptures as the seventy interpreted them; for having spoken them previously as you have them, I was making a test of you, how you are already disposed in your opinion. For saying the scripture which says: Woe to them, because they devise a wicked plan against themselves, saying: Let us remove the righteous one, because he is troublesome to us, as the seventy interpreted it, I praised; Let us bind the righteous one, because he is troublesome to us, which you said, having said what you wish to be said. But you have done something else, and you do not seem to me to have listened attentively to the words. But since now the day is about to come to an end, for the sun is already in the west, and adding something to what has been said, I will stop; but this very thing was also said to me in what was said, and it seems to me to be right to elaborate on it again.

pass_b_english: Brothers, do not speak any evil against the crucified one, nor mock his bruises, by which it is possible for all to be healed, just as we also have been healed. It is a good thing, if you are persuaded by these words, to circumcise your hardness of heart—a hardness you do not possess because of your own opinion, since it was given as a sign, not as a work of righteousness, as the words compel. Therefore, having come to agreement, do not rail against the Son of God, nor, by obeying Pharisee teachers, ever despise the King of Israel, just as your synagogue rulers teach after the prayer. For if the one who touches things not pleasing to God is like one who touches the daughter of God, how much more so the one who touches the Beloved. That this one is he has been sufficiently demonstrated. When they fell silent, I said: 'I, my friends, now speak the scriptures as the Seventy interpreted them; for having spoken them to you previously just as you possess them, I was testing you to see how your opinion was already disposed.' For when I recited the scripture that says: 'Woe to them, because they devise a wicked plan against themselves,' saying, 'Let us remove the righteous one, because he is troublesome to us,' as the Seventy interpreted it, I assented; but you said, 'Let us bind the righteous one, because he is troublesome to us,' speaking exactly what you wished to say. You have done something else, and it does not seem to me that you have listened attentively to the words. But since the day is now about to end—for the sun is already in the west—I will cease after adding one thing to what has been said; yet this very thing was also spoken to me within what was said, and it seems right to me to elaborate on it again. (Isaiah 3:10-11)

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the nuances of the Greek text, particularly the distinction between 'Ἄρωμεν' (let us remove) and 'Δήσωμεν' (let us bind), which is central to the argument regarding the Seventy's interpretation. Pass A and Pass B are consistent with the Greek. The scripture citation (Isaiah 3:10-11) correctly identifies the allusion in the text.
